subject: Tie-breaker criteria & technical probes — next tests for MedIQ bakeoff
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@mediq.com>, Claire Wu <claire.wu@mediq.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Tie-breaker criteria & technical probes — next tests for MedIQ bakeoff

Hi Sanjay / Claire —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned acceptance criteria for the bakeoff window. I focused this on the three items you emphasized: latency guarantees under concurrent traffic, predictable cost per 1k tokens, and data isolation/retention.

Summary of pain & goals (as we heard them):
- Real-time clinical assistants need 95th percentile latency < 150ms for 256-token responses at 10 qps.
- Keep per-token inference cost within your target threshold (~$0.0009/token).
- No cross-tenant KV leakage; audit logs for inference events for HIPAA compliance.

Proposed tie-breaker framework (please confirm weights):
1) Performance (40%) — 95th percentile latency at target QPS, warm/hot cache behavior.
2) Reliability & fallbacks (25%) — graceful degradation to smaller model variant when capacity is constrained.
3) Security & compliance (20%) — KMS/HSM integration, auditability, data residency.
4) Economics (15%) — cost/token at expected traffic patterns and caching efficiency.

Technical probes we propose to run in the bakeoff window (I added owners):
- Latency ramp (Aditya): run 1–20 qps sweep with synthetic prompts, record P50/P95/P99, and tail spikes with prolonged KV cache disabled/enabled.
- KV persistence check (Monica): validate prefix caching across requests and after instance restarts; confirm cache TTL behavior.
- Multi-tenant isolation smoke (Aditya + Monica): interleaved requests across two tenant keys and make sure no KV leakage or cross-contamination occurs.
- Cost modeling (Hannah): capture tokens, GPU utilization estimates, and compute an effective cost/token with/without caching.

Attachments: I attached a comparison matrix (mediq_comparison_matrix_v2.xlsx) and a short POC checklist (poc-smoke-checklist.pdf) with the exact commands we propose to run. Also linked a shared Drive sheet for live results.

Please reply with any weight changes for the tie-breaker, or additional probes you want included. If this looks good, we'll book the test window Tues-Fri next week (11–14 Aug) and kick off infra prep on Monday.

Next immediate asks:
- Sanjay: confirm the weighted criteria or send edits by EOD Wed.
- Claire: confirm the preferred test days / blackout windows for your environment.
- Aditya / Monica: confirm you can run the probes and estimate time to prepare infra.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@mediq.com>, Claire Wu <claire.wu@mediq.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tie-breaker criteria & technical probes — next tests for MedIQ bakeoff

All — quick note from my side. Framework looks good; two adjustments I recommend:
1) Move some weight from Economics -> Reliability: in practice performance variability is the real tie breaker here. Proposed split: Performance 45%, Reliability 30%, Security 15%, Economics 10%.
2) Add a routing/fallback probe: measure latency when we intentionally route to a cheaper region/model variant to validate graceful quality/latency tradeoff. This is a small add but can be decisive if costs are close.

I can own the ramp and routing probe; I'll need 1 full day to provision the test harness (I estimate Mon afternoon).

- Aditya

From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@mediq.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Tie-breaker criteria & technical probes — next tests for MedIQ bakeoff

Thanks Hannah — this is super helpful and captures the discussion.

A few quick confirmations from our side:
- We're comfortable with your adjusted probe list; the performance and reliability weight shift Aditya suggested looks reasonable to us.
- Blackout window: please avoid 12–18 Aug (we have a vendor freeze). Can you instead target 11–13 Aug for the active tests and leave 14 Aug as a buffer?
- For the routing/fallback probe please include an explanation of expected quality deltas (short bullet) so our clinical team can understand degradation patterns.

We'll sign off once we see the final schedule and the Drive sheet populated with test commands.

Thanks —
Sanjay
VP Product, MedIQ
Sanjay Reddy <sanjay@mediq.com>

Perfect — thanks for the quick responses. Finalized plan below (we'll also update the shared Drive):

Schedule: 11 Aug (ramp + KV persistence), 12 Aug (routing/fallback + isolation smoke), 13 Aug (cost modeling + buffer validation). 14 Aug reserved as a contingency day.
Owners: Aditya (ramp + routing), Monica (KV persistence + isolation smoke), Hannah (cost modeling + results sheet).
Deliverables by EOD 10 Aug: updated comparison matrix, Drive sheet with exact commands, and a short one-page note on expected quality delta for the fallback routing (will include sample response pairs).

On Mon we'll run a quick infra readiness check and confirm that the test harness can hit the target QPS without warmup gaps. I've attached the POC checklist and the comparison matrix again for easy reference.

Looking forward — I'll set up the calendar block and include the Zoom link.

Best,
Hannah
